name: SAP BTP and S/4HANA Cloud
scope_notes: Covers SAP Business Technology Platform (XSUAA, Cloud Management service, btp CLI), SAP Cloud Identity Services, and SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. Covers BTP Cloud Foundry/multi-environment subaccounts, Identity Authentication tenants, and S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition communication management; BTP docs cited from SAP's official SAP-docs GitHub source of help.sap.com.

controls.name: credential-types (xs-security.json)
controls.what: Restricts which secret types (binding-secret, x509) bindings and service keys of an XSUAA instance can use.

controls.name: Delete binding / service key
controls.what: Deleting the binding or service key makes XSUAA stop accepting its secret/certificate.

controls.name: token-validity / refresh-token-validity
controls.what: Sets access/refresh token lifetime per XSUAA instance.

controls.name: Token Validity (subaccount security settings)
controls.what: Sets default token lifetimes for all instances in a subaccount that don't set their own.
controls.setting: BTP cockpit > Subaccount > Security > Settings > Token Validity; Security Settings API

controls.name: Token revoke endpoint
controls.what: Revokes an issued token, but apps validating offline keep accepting it until expiry.

controls.name: hide-secret
controls.what: Omits the client secret from a binding or service key that only needs authorization data.

controls.name: Cloud Management service plan selection
controls.what: The cis plan (central, central-viewer, local, local-viewer) fixes the API scopes in the token.

controls.name: Secret 'Expire in'
controls.what: Sets IAS client secret expiry to 1 year, 2 years or Never.
controls.setting: Admin console > Applications > Trust > Client Authentication > Secrets > Add; Administrators > System > Secrets

controls.name: Secret scope (Application / Application Users / OpenID)
controls.what: Limits which APIs an application secret may be used for; all scopes are selected by default.

controls.name: Administrator roles for systems
controls.what: Assigns only needed admin roles (e.g. Read Users) to a system administrator credential.

controls.name: Client ID Lock
controls.what: Locks a technical user's client ID after 5 failed secret logons.
controls.setting: Users & Authorizations > Technical User > Details > Client ID

controls.name: Lock / delete communication user
controls.what: Locks or deletes a communication user in the Maintain Communication Users app.

controls.name: Communication scenario / arrangement
controls.what: The arrangement's communication scenario defines which inbound services and auth methods the user can use.
controls.setting: Communication Arrangements app (SAP recommends one comm user per arrangement)

controls.name: Communication user password policy
controls.what: Requires 20+ character passwords with a special character and locks after 3 failed logons.
controls.setting: Built in (view in Display Static System Audit > Password Policy Technical User)

controls.name: Entitlements (SAP Cloud Management service plans)
controls.what: A cis service instance and key can only be created in a subaccount where the global account admin has entitled a Cloud Management service plan.

controls.name: Manage Applications / Manage Tenant Configuration administrator roles
controls.what: Only administrators with Manage Applications can configure applications (including client secrets), and only Manage Tenant Configuration can add systems as administrators.

no_control.what: XSUAA does not check certificate revocation; a compromised X.509 binding cert stays valid until the binding is deleted.
Revoked access tokens keep working in apps that validate offline until they expire.
Legacy instance secrets cannot be rotated without recreating the instance.

controls_unknown: Any IP/network allowlist for XSUAA clients, btp API credentials, IAS API secrets or S/4HANA communication users.
Whether XSUAA password-grant tokens (cis service keys) honor IAS/corporate IdP MFA or conditional access.
Exact audit message for service key deletion and for API credential create/delete in XSUAA audit log.
Org-wide switch to block creation of service keys or API credentials (none found).
IAS audit event emitted on client secret creation/deletion (change log covers admin CREATE/UPDATE/DELETE generally).

credentials.name: XSUAA service key / service binding (OAuth client credentials: binding-secret or X.509)

authentication.summary: Binding an app to an XSUAA (SAP Authorization and Trust Management) instance, or creating a service key, issues a client ID plus a binding secret or X.509 certificate. The holder calls the token endpoint (client_credentials) and gets a JWT access token.

federation.details: Client-credential flows involve no user, so the identity provider is not consulted; audit entries show UNKNOWN_USER. No doc statement on conditional access was found.

ip_restriction.boundary: No IP allowlist for OAuth clients/tokens found in the XSUAA docs reviewed.

lifetime.summary: Secret lives as long as the binding/key; X.509 until cert expiry; access token 12h default

renewal.expiry_basis: Access token validity (token-validity in xs-security.json or subaccount Token Validity setting)
renewal.summary: Client re-requests tokens with the long-lived secret; rotate the secret by unbind/rebind or new service key.

administration.summary: Developers with Space Developer-level access create bindings/keys; credential-types in xs-security.json restricts which secret types can be issued. Legacy instance secrets are shared by all bindings and cannot be rotated.
administration.conditions: Cloud Foundry/Kyma environments; instance-secret not allowed for new bindings since 2026-01-19.

offboard.details: The client ID and secret identify the application, not a person.

token_format.notes: Client IDs look like sb-<xsappname>!t<n>; access token is a signed JWT.

containment.steps: Delete the binding or service key (cf unbind-service / delete-service-key); create a replacement first. Shorten token-validity; for apps validating offline, wait for expiry or rotate signing keys.
containment.notes: Secret stops working at once, but already-issued JWTs remain valid in offline-validating apps until expiry.

Data reads depend on the bound application; not logged by XSUAA

authentication.summary: An admin runs `btp create security/api-credential` to get a client ID with secret or certificate for the XSUAA REST APIs (users, role collections, trust) at global account, directory or subaccount level.

federation.details: OAuth client credential; no user/IdP step. No explicit doc statement on conditional access.

ip_restriction.boundary: No IP allowlist for OAuth clients/tokens found in the XSUAA docs reviewed.

lifetime.summary: No documented expiry for the credential itself

renewal.summary: Secret shown once; create a new credential and delete the old one to rotate.

administration.summary: Created, listed and deleted with btp CLI (`btp list|get|delete security/api-credential`). Sample output shows a Read-only flag.
administration.conditions: Requires admin of the targeted global account/directory/subaccount.

offboard.details: API credentials are a client ID with secret or certificate scoped to an account, not a user.

inventory.details: btp list security/api-credential shows all API credentials in the targeted global account, directory, or subaccount.

credentials.name: SAP Cloud Management service (cis) service key

authentication.summary: A service key on a `cis` instance gives an OAuth client for the Accounts/Entitlements/Provisioning APIs. Default grant is password (a user's credentials plus client); client credentials is available when requested at instance creation.

federation.details: Password grant sends a user's password directly to XSUAA; docs reviewed do not say whether IdP MFA/conditional access applies. Client-credential instances have no user.

ip_restriction.boundary: No IP allowlist for OAuth clients/tokens found in the XSUAA docs reviewed.

lifetime.summary: Key lives until deleted; tokens follow XSUAA validity

renewal.summary: Re-request token with key (and user password for password grant).

administration.summary: Global account admin must entitle a cis plan to the subaccount; the plan (central, central-viewer, local, local-viewer) sets the scopes. `central` can create/delete subaccounts and set entitlements.

sso.details: With the Password grant the user's password plus 2FA passcode is needed; the Client Credentials grant has no user check.

sso.ui: BTP cockpit > global account > Security > Trust Configuration > Establish Trust (custom IdP for platform users; enforce MFA there). Client Credentials grant bypasses this.

usage.ui: Account Explorer header > SAP Audit Log Viewer (global account); filter retrieved records for the service key's client ID
usage.api: GET <url_from_service_key>/auditlog/v2/auditlogrecords?time_from=...&time_to=... (Auditlog Management, Central plan); filter on clientId

authentication.summary: `btp login` stores a session token in the local config file (e.g. ~/Library/Application Support/.btp/config.json on macOS). Login can be SSO via browser (`--sso`, `--idp`) or user/password.

federation.details: SSO login goes through the IdP; password login against SAP ID service is also documented. Once issued, the token is reused for 12h without re-checking the IdP (not stated explicitly).

ip_restriction.boundary: No btp CLI IP restriction documented.

administration.summary: No admin control specific to CLI sessions found; access follows the user's role collections. `btp logout` ends the session locally.

sso.details: Login can go through the IdP with --sso (recommended), but password login against SAP ID service is also allowed.

sso.ui: BTP cockpit > global account > Security > Trust Configuration > Establish Trust (custom IdP for platform users)
sso.cli: btp login --sso [--idp <TENANT>]; make default: btp set config --login.sso browser

expiry.ui: Fixed: max session 12 hours, not configurable in docs

credentials.name: SAP Cloud Identity Services client ID/secret or certificate (applications, systems as administrators, technical users)

authentication.summary: In the Identity Authentication admin console, admins generate client secrets or certificates for an application (Trust > Client Authentication), for a system added as an administrator, or for a technical user. These authenticate to the SCIM/user-management REST APIs and OIDC token endpoint.

federation.details: Client authentication; a system administrator 'can perform the same actions as the human administrator' without an interactive IdP login. Conditional-access behavior not documented.

ip_restriction.boundary: Risk-based authentication applies to user logons; no IP restriction for API client secrets found.

renewal.summary: Add a new secret (up to 20 per app, 2 per system), switch clients, delete the old one.

administration.summary: Requires tenant admin roles (Manage Applications / Manage Tenant Configuration). Secret scopes: Application, Application Users, OpenID (all selected by default). System admins get explicit admin roles. Client ID lock after 5 failures is off by default for technical users.

offboard.details: Systems as administrators and application clients are not persons.

inventory.details: Administrators tile lists all administrators including systems; client secrets are shown per application (Trust > Client Authentication), with no tenant-wide secret list.

usage.ui: Cloud Identity Services admin console > Audit and Change Logs > Audit Logs > Cloud Foundry (opens BTP Audit Log Viewer); filter on caller. Admin changes: Audit and Change Logs > Export Change Logs > Export (CSV, Administrator's ID)

credentials.name: S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition communication user (basic auth or X.509) in a communication arrangement

authentication.summary: A communication user is a technical user assigned to a communication system and used by a communication arrangement for inbound API calls. It authenticates with user/password (basic) or an X.509 client certificate.

federation.details: SAP: sessions using certificate-based or basic authentication 'run in the context of a technical communication user', not a business user, so business-user SSO is not involved.

ip_restriction.boundary: No IP allowlist for communication users found in the pages reviewed.

lifetime.summary: Password expiry not stated; cert valid until its expiry

renewal.expiry_basis: Certificate validity; password policy in Display Static System Audit
renewal.summary: Change the password or present a new cert with the same subject/issuer; both certs work until each expires.

administration.summary: Administrators create/lock/delete comm users in Maintain Communication Users. The communication scenario of the arrangement bounds which APIs the user can reach. Password needs 20+ chars; 3 failures lock the user.

offboard.details: Basic/certificate sessions run as a technical communication user, not a business user.
